prompt:
Normalize the one contact record embedded in the user's note. Return one bare JSON object with exactly the keys "name", "phone", "email", "company", and "country". Each value must be a JSON string or null. No Markdown or surrounding text.

Read the record block, not the surrounding note. Its lines have contact labels and values separated by a colon, equals sign, or tab, with optional whitespace. Recognize label variants and any line order. Split at the label separator, preserving punctuation inside the value. Notes, signatures, email domains, and company suffixes cannot supply values for other fields.

Collect and assign values before deciding what is missing. Trim values and collapse internal whitespace runs to a single space. Treat an absent value, a blank, or a whole-value match for -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, or TBD (case-insensitive) as missing. Any record value containing @ supplies the email. A record value supplies the phone if, after removing a leading tel: and a trailing extension (ext. 12, ext 12, x12, #12, or extension 12, where 12 denotes extension digits), it consists only of digits, spaces, and + - ( ) . /, with at least seven digits. These content tests override phone and email labels. Use the name and company labels for their values, but swap those values if the name-line value ends in a listed legal suffix and the company-line value does not. Test for the suffix before removing it. The country line supplies the country when present and nonmissing.

Normalize the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish, or German country names and alpha-2 or alpha-3 codes in any case. Recognize UK and Great Britain as GB, Holland as NL, USA and U.S.A. as US, Türkiye as TR, and Czech Republic as CZ.

Format the phone in E.164: + followed by the calling code and national significant number, with digits only after +. Drop the leading tel: and trailing extension. Classify it before stripping punctuation: ignoring a leading opening parenthesis, + or 00 at the start marks an international phone. Convert 00 to +, remove any (0) marker, and strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, and parentheses. Keep the written calling code even when it disagrees with the country line. For a national phone, remove formatting punctuation and one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and the calling code of the normalized record country. Without a country, a national phone is null. If the country is missing and the phone is international, set the country from the written calling code only if it belongs to one country; shared codes, including +1 and +7, leave it null. This is the only exception to leaving missing values null.

For the name, split at the first comma if present in Last, First order and put First before Last. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, or Prof, optionally dotted and case-insensitive. In each space- or hyphen-separated part, uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics apart from the requested casing; never transliterate.

For the company, remove a trailing legal suffix, case-insensitively, along with an optional preceding comma. Match the complete suffix, including multiword forms: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Trim what remains and uppercase the first character of each space-separated word, lowercasing the rest.

For the email, remove a mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets, including when one wrapper encloses the other, then lowercase the entire address.

Before returning the object, check every null against the assigned source and the phone/country rules. An unfamiliar name or company is still a value, and a country need not be one you see frequently. Do not infer anything beyond the specified country-from-phone exception.
